**0087 round two (`9196ca3`), dc's verdict: OK to close, with one gap that I think should be closed first. Your call.**

Run on scratch copies of HEAD `3c22861` (`git archive`), each with its own TMPDIR. All mutants are at `lib/gatecmd:143`, the builtin-fn opener, with `-f 0087` over `dispatch.bats`. The script is `scratchpad/mut0087/run.sh`.

| mutant                                         | result                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `"${@}"` in place of ARGS                      | killed (class arm)          |
| ARGS plus `"${@}"`                             | killed (class arm)          |
| ARGS plus `"${@:1}"`                           | killed (class arm)          |
| ARGS, then `"$@"` on the next line             | killed (class arm)          |
| mine: ARGS plus `$*`, `"$*"`, `$@`, `"${@:2}"` | all killed (class arm)      |
| mine: argv laundered through a local array   | **LIVE** (see below)        |

The live one is `local -a _raw=("$@")` above the call, then ARGS plus `"${_raw[@]}"`. It passes all 84 tests in `dispatch.bats`, and every `purge` or `builtin` arm across `tests/unit` (22/22).

**The gap: every kill comes from the class arm alone.** Even the first mutant, which throws ARGS away completely, passes all four behavioural 0087 arms, because those arms drive the command-level gate and not the builtin-fn one. So **no behavioural arm covers the builtin-fn gate at all.** Laundering the argv through an array is outside what a lexical reader can see, which is the limit you would expect, but here nothing behind the class arm catches it.

**Proposed fix:** one arm with a stub builtin fn that has a `_gateflags` hook. Call it with `--purge` and an ordinary argument, then assert two things: the fn receives the ordinary argument only, and prior pairs are purged. It should go red on my mutants 1 and 8.

HEAD control: 22/22 green. One other thing: the tree has uncommitted work of yours in `lib/runlog` and `runlog.bats` (row 2's `</dev/null`), and I have not touched it.

Next: the WP-03 review, which will include `release_git_remote` at 7c4d5d8.
